pins.title: Hyundai Motor Group Raises U.S. Strategic Investment to US$26 Billion for 2025–2028
pins.description: The group increased its U.S. investment commitment by US$5 billion to US$26 billion for 2025–2028, covering automotive capacity, a Louisiana steel mill and robotics. This replaces the earlier US$21 billion plan.
points: US$26 billion is the updated total commitment; the incremental increase is US$5 billion over the March 2025 plan.
Investment covers steel production, expanded Hyundai and Kia vehicle capacity, and a robotics facility designed for 30,000 units annually.
The group expects around 25,000 direct jobs by 2028. These are announced targets, rather than completed expenditure.
pins.gap: Official release and linked media-kit section checked; release supplies a generic newsroom image rather than a project photograph.

pins.title: Hyundai Motor Group Commits US$15.5 Billion to India for 2026–2032
pins.description: The seven-year strategic commitment covers Hyundai and Kia manufacturing expansion, R&D, local suppliers and future mobility. About US$700 million within the US$15.5 billion plan is allocated to the Indian R&D center and testing track.
points: Announced on October 13, 2026, the US$15.5 billion investment runs from 2026 through 2032.
Approximately US$700 million is planned for the Indian R&D center, including a vehicle testing track; this is part of the overall commitment.
A dedicated Indian investment entity will coordinate capital deployment and partnerships. Manufacturing, supplier localization, charging and recycling are among the investment areas.

pins.title: Toyota Announces Up to US$10 Billion in Additional U.S. Investment Over Five Years
pins.description: Toyota announced up to US$10 billion of additional U.S. investment over five years. The commitment was presented alongside the opening of its nearly US$14 billion North Carolina battery plant; the two figures describe different investment scopes.
points: The November 13 global announcement states an additional U.S. investment ceiling of US$10 billion over the next five years.
Toyota separately described the North Carolina battery plant as a nearly US$14 billion investment, with up to 5,100 jobs.
Later Kentucky and Indiana allocations belong within this five-year program; they should not be added to its headline ceiling.
images: North Carolina battery-plant opening accompanying the U.S. investment announcement
pins.gap: Official global release and linked U.S. press gallery checked. Global release date is November 13; U.S. opening release is dated November 12.

pins.period: Allocation announced March 2026 within the five-year U.S. program
pins.title: Toyota Allocates US$1 Billion to Kentucky and Indiana Manufacturing
pins.description: Toyota allocated US$800 million to Kentucky and US$200 million to Indiana. The US$1 billion total is part of the previously announced U.S. program of up to US$10 billion, supporting electric-vehicle preparation and vehicle assembly capacity.
points: Kentucky receives US$800 million to prepare for a second battery electric vehicle and increase Camry and RAV4 assembly capacity.
Indiana receives US$200 million to expand Grand Highlander capacity.
The combined US$1 billion allocation sits within Toyota’s November 2025 five-year commitment of up to US$10 billion.

pins.period: Multi-year expansion; no single completion date stated
pins.title: GlobalFoundries Announces US$16 Billion U.S. Manufacturing and R&D Plan
pins.description: GlobalFoundries outlined US$16 billion for manufacturing, advanced packaging and R&D in New York and Vermont. The plan combines existing expansion commitments exceeding US$13 billion with an additional US$3 billion for technology development.
points: The US$16 billion aggregate includes previously announced U.S. expansion plans rather than representing US$16 billion entirely in new spending.
An additional US$3 billion supports advanced R&D, packaging, silicon photonics and gallium nitride technologies.
The program spans New York and Vermont manufacturing and advanced packaging capabilities; the release gives no single completion deadline.
pins.gap: Official release and site image metadata checked; generic branding and unrelated related-story images were excluded.

pins.period: First fab targeted for 2029; second fab timing unspecified
pins.title: Japan Initiative Provides Up to US$21 Billion for Two GlobalFoundries-Operated New York Fabs
pins.description: GlobalFoundries was selected to operate two new Malta, New York fabs under a U.S.–Japan initiative providing up to US$21 billion. Japan supplies the investment; GlobalFoundries supplies technology and operations. The first fab is expected online in 2029.
points: Up to US$21 billion is initiative funding from Japan, rather than an equivalent GlobalFoundries corporate cash commitment.
Approximately US$10 billion would accelerate the first 300mm fab, targeted for 2029; another approximately US$10 billion would finance a second fab.
The funding ceiling and approximate fab allocations are distinct figures. The release does not establish that the full ceiling is additional to every earlier expansion commitment.
pins.gap: Official announcement and press photo metadata checked; no clearly captioned project photograph in article body.

pins.title: Siemens Invests US$285 Million in Texas and California Electrical Manufacturing
pins.description: Siemens announced US$285 million for electrical-equipment manufacturing facilities in Fort Worth, Texas and Pomona, California, with more than 900 expected jobs. The separate headline of more than US$10 billion also includes software and acquisition activity.
points: US$285 million covers two electrical-products manufacturing facilities serving infrastructure and data-center demand.
Siemens expected more than 900 skilled manufacturing jobs from the facilities.
The release’s broader investment headline exceeds US$10 billion and includes the planned Altair acquisition; it is not a factory-only capital expenditure figure.

pins.period: Cumulative over the preceding five years; projects coming online in 2026
pins.title: Siemens Reports US$1 Billion U.S. Manufacturing Investment Milestone
pins.description: Siemens reported US$1 billion of domestic manufacturing investments over five years, supporting more than 2,200 jobs. The cumulative milestone spans electrical infrastructure and passenger rail projects, with facilities coming online during 2026.
points: The US$1 billion figure is a cumulative five-year manufacturing milestone, rather than a new one-day US$1 billion commitment.
Projects support power equipment, industrial infrastructure and passenger rail, with investments adding more than 2,200 jobs.
This cumulative milestone should not be mechanically added to earlier individual Siemens factory announcements.
pins.gap: Official article image and linked project imagery checked. Hero is general industrial imagery; excluded to avoid presenting it as a specific new factory.

pins.period: Opening targeted for late 2027 in the announcement
pins.title: Eli Lilly Commits US$4.5 Billion to the Indiana Medicine Foundry
pins.description: Lilly announced US$4.5 billion for a Lebanon, Indiana center combining manufacturing-process research with production of clinical-trial medicines. The announcement targeted a late-2027 opening and around 400 full-time jobs.
points: The US$4.5 billion Medicine Foundry commitment was announced on October 2, 2024.
The site is designed to develop manufacturing methods and supply clinical trials, with technologies later transferred to commercial sites.
Late 2027 was the announced opening target. This historical commitment is distinct from Lilly’s additional US$4.5 billion allocation across two other Lebanon sites in May 2026.

pins.period: Additional commitment announced May 2026; Lebanon API opening targeted for 2027
pins.title: Eli Lilly Adds US$4.5 Billion Across Two Indiana Manufacturing Sites
pins.description: Lilly committed an additional US$4.5 billion to Lebanon API and Lebanon Advanced Therapies, taking Indiana capital expansion commitments since 2020 above US$21 billion. It also opened its dedicated genetic-medicine manufacturing facility.
points: The additional US$4.5 billion supports Lebanon API and Lebanon Advanced Therapies, two of the campus’s three planned sites.
The company reported total Indiana expansion commitments of more than US$21 billion since 2020; this cumulative figure includes earlier commitments.
Lebanon Advanced Therapies opened on May 6, 2026. Lilly stated a 2027 opening target for Lebanon API; the Medicine Foundry remains a separate campus project.
pins.gap: Official investor announcement and media links checked; only a generic laboratory hero and corporate logo were available, so no site-specific photograph added.
